root_idea.summary: The root denotes washing as an act of purification and cleansing: removing dirt or other matter by water.
root_idea.development: From physical washing, the lexical family extends to complete bodily washing, washing substances and wash-water, matter washed away, and several specialized or figurative uses.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form I perfect citation form.
Displayed under the normalized Form VIII perfect citation form.
A distinct Quranic noun with a specialized Hell-related meaning.
A substantivized passive participle functioning as a distinct Quranic noun.

senses.definition: To wash something by making water run over it so as to remove dirt, filth, or similar matter.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quran, used in the imperative for washing specified body parts in ritual purification.

senses.definition: To wash oneself, especially by washing the whole body with water.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic occurrence refers to bodily washing in the context of purification.

senses.definition: The foul matter washed from the flesh and bodies of the inmates of Hell.
senses.usage_conditions: The primary Quranic interpretation is wash-off from their bodies, flesh, or wounds.

senses.definition: A food of the inmates of Hell, explained as matter or flesh cooked by the fire and fallen from their bodies.
senses.usage_conditions: An alternative exegetical interpretation of the Quranic term, not a separate occurrence.

senses.definition: A species of tree in Hell.
senses.usage_conditions: An interpretation attributed in the lexical discussion to a particular exegetical authority.
An alternative interpretation of the Quranic term.
In the Quranic expression, it denotes a bathing place or spring.
The Quranic noun may refer to the water in which or with which one bathes; the occurrence is independently located at 38:42.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cleanse someone from sin or moral impurity.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use based on physical washing and cleansing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become free of, or get clear of, the consequences of an affair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative idiom associated with becoming clean or finished with something.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a horse, to sweat or become suffused with sweat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized intransitive use said of a horse.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To have sexual intercourse.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional figurative use of غَسَلَ in the construction غَسَلَ المرأةَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a stallion, to cover a female repeatedly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized use referring to frequent mating.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To beat and cause pain with a whip.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative or specialized transitive use with a whip as instrument.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a stallion, to cover a female much or often.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form IV specialized use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become washed or washed off.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A quasi-passive intransitive use of the root.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To smear, daub, or sprinkle oneself copiously with perfume.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized Form VIII use with perfume.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To request or undergo a prescribed washing ritual performed by another person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional Form X use in the treatment associated with the evil eye.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Washing; the act of making water run over something to remove dirt or filth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The verbal noun of غَسَلَ; authorities differ over its distinction from غُسْلٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A complete washing of the whole person, including a ritual bath.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Classically associated with major impurity, childbirth, Friday prayer, and washing the dead.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A preparation or substance used for washing or dressing the head and hair, including plant materials, potash, perfume, or similar ingredients.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term may refer to a head-wash preparation and to materials used in grooming the hair.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A man who has sexual intercourse frequently.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized nominal use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A single act of washing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural is غَسَلَاتٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Figuratively, earnings or means of livelihood.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use in the expression describing a city built by its builders' earnings.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A quality of facial beauty or freshness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the expression عَلَى وَجْهِهِ غِسْلَةٌ, describing a face without fatness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A name for the wolf.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An appellation rather than a general noun for the animal.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who covers or mates much, or does so without impregnating.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied especially to a stallion and also to a man.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Water or another substance used for washing the body, head, hands, or garments.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It may refer especially to a small quantity of wash-water or to plant-based washing materials.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Washed; something that has been washed, including a dead body.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used adjectivally of things and substantivally in some contexts.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Clothes or similar items gathered together to be washed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A later or current nominal use of the washed material.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The water or liquid resulting from washing, including matter extracted or washed from a thing; by extension, an infusion steeped from it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term can denote either the wash-water or material carried away by it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A plant that grows in places exuding water and producing salt.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It is also described as a species of tree.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A washer of clothes or of the dead.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The feminine is formed with ة.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A washer of the dead.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized occupational noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A species of tree.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separate nominal sense of the same form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Potash or the alkaline plant from which it is prepared, used as a washing substance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Identified with أُشْنَان and related glasswort plants.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place in which the dead are washed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A place noun with the plural مَغَاسِلُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A vessel in which a thing is washed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An instrument or container noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Figuratively, speech stripped of refined expressions or allusions; hence speech that is plain, trimmed, or pruned.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A metaphorical extension of something washed free of additions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A tank or basin, especially one described as made of copper.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized Classical Arabic usage distinct from the Quranic bathing-place and bathing-water senses.

cautions: The Quranic noun غِسْلِين has several recorded exegetical interpretations; the primary wash-off interpretation is kept distinct from alternative food, tree, and intense-heat interpretations.

A Lane Quran citation in the غَسُولٌ discussion is printed in historical form as “xxxviii. 41” and is not converted into a modern verse location; the Quranic location 38:42 for مُغْتَسَل is established independently by QAC and Mufradat.
unassigned_or_ambiguous_evidence: Lane entry 29299 contains an abbreviated or omitted expression associated with its historical Quran citation, so that citation is not used to identify a separate modern Quran occurrence or to override the independently secured QAC headword مُغْتَسَل.
